steps.text: Beat together sugar, butter, cream cheese, egg yolk, salt, almond extract, and vanilla in a large bowl with an electric mixer until smooth.
Gradually mix in flour until dough comes together.
Divide dough into thirds and form each piece into a disk. Wrap tightly with plastic wrap and refrigerate, 8 hours to overnight.
When ready to bake, preheat the oven to 375 degrees F (190 degrees C).
Working with one disk at a time, roll dough on a lightly floured surface to an 1/8-inch thickness; keep other disks refrigerated until ready to roll.
Cut dough into desired shapes with lightly floured cookie cutters. Place cookies 1 inch apart onto ungreased baking sheets.
Bake in the preheated oven until cookies are light golden brown, 7 to 10 minutes, switching racks halfway through. Remove from the oven and transfer cookies to wire racks.

raw_recipe.headline: Cream Cheese Sugar Cookies
raw_recipe.description: These sugar cookies with cream cheese are soft, chewy, and simple to make by rolling out the chilled dough, cutting out desired shapes, and icing.

video.description: Beautiful and delicate looking cream cheese sugar cookies will delight your taste buds and your guests will love them! Or have your kids decorate for a festive, fun, and delicious activity!

review.reviewBody: Wonderful Cream Cheese Cookies! My recipe is a little different however. If you want your dough to be perfect you MUST use real butter and make sure it is unsalted. I use Land O Lakes. I use 8oz. of cream cheese, not 3oz. 1 1/2 cup sugar, 1 cup of unsalted butter, 1 8oz cream cheese, 1 egg, 1 tsp vanilla, 1/2 tsp almond extract, 3 1/2 cup flour and 1 tsp baking powder. I've never had problems getting these to roll out after chilling the appropriate amount of time. They bake easy and taste wonderful. I use royal icing to decorate. They make great gifts as long as I can get them out of the house before everyone in my family eats them!!

I used the suggested changes of another user. I used 1 cup unsalted real butter, 8oz. of cream cheese, 1 1/2 cup sugar, 1 egg, 1 tsp vanilla, 1/2 tsp almond extract, 3 1/2 cup flour and 1 tsp baking powder. Very easy to work with and tasted great!

Cherish and other reviewers suggested the following changes and these cookies came out perfect!
1 1/2 cup sugar, 1 cup of unsalted butter, 1 8oz cream cheese, 1 egg, 1 tsp vanilla, 1/2 tsp almond extract, 3 1/2 cup flour and 1 tsp baking powder


I might have only used 1cup sugar though, can't exactly remember.

But- these cookies were absolutely delicious! They were soft, not too sweet, perfect flavourful (I could eat them without frosting, though its even better with it). 

This is one of the best and easiest recipes I've tried on allrecipes. This will be my go to sugar cookie recipe from now on.

Frosting:
*I hate sickly sweet frosting, and began to follow the Sugar Cookie Frosting recipe on this website as reviewers said it wasn't too sweet. I hated it-- it was waay to sweet, so I modified it. Here is my frosting recipe:

1cup unsalted butter,
3-4 cups icing (confectioners) sugar (start with 2-3cups and add more until you get your desired sweetness)
8-10TBSP milk
1pkg (8oz) cream cheese
2/3 tsp almond extract
1 1/2tsp Vanilla extract
Food colouring

Beat all ingredients together. Its perfectly flavoured and not overly sweet. If you let the frosting dry overnight on the cookies, it will be stackable, but the frosting does not completely harden.

Excellent cookie recipe, it was just what I was looking for. It makes soft cookies that aren't too sweet that melt in your mouth. I did change the recipe slightly. I double the recipe because I used 8 oz of cheese instead of 3 oz and I didn't put salt in the cookies. The dough I made was perfect after 8 hours in the fridge. I let the dough thaw a little so it was easier to roll out for about 30 minutes. The cookies cut-out nicely and didn't need to flour the rolling pin. I baked my cookies until I saw a golden edge appear in the oven around 8-9 minutes in the oven @ 375 degrees. All I have to say is I made over 30 cookies and they were mostly gone with a day and half. Definitely recommend this recipe to anyone.

I have made these cookies for years! I triple the recipe and use an 8 oz package of cream cheese. I don’t change any other ingredients. I roll them out a little thicker because that’s how we like them. I brush with egg white and sprinkle with colored sugar before baking. The dough is never sticky and easy to roll out. I’m not allowed to make any other sugar cookie.

I will definitely make this recipe again, but there were a few adjustments I made. First, I added more vanilla about a TBSP) and less almond extract, simply based on my flavor preference, and I also added about a 1/2 c more sugar and an extra ounce (about 4 oz total) of cream cheese after reading another review that the recipe was bland. I also did not add as much flour as it called for because I often find sugar cookies too dry. I mixed until the dough looked dry, not sticky, but not overly floury. Finally, we did not use them for cutouts so I cannot attest to how they would work with cookie cutters. We rolled them into little balls and dipped them in different sprinkles, then baked. They were amazing! They are so soft and they have a wonderful flavor, sweet, but not too sweet, and the cream cheese adds a subtle richness to the overall taste. I will definitely make these again. Maybe next time I'll try them with cutouts, but I will likely need to use more flour for cutouts.

I love the suggested changes cookie. Things I would like to add to help an amatures like me. Mix 8oz cream cheese, 1 1/2 cups of sugar and 1 cup unsalted butter. Mix till properly creamed... the sugar becomes one with the butter. Then add 1 egg, 1 teaspoon vanilla and 1/2 tsp of almond extract mix again. Then add 3 1/2 cups of flour 1 tsp of baking powder. I also did a chocolate raspberry filling. Heat a 1/4 of whip cream to just a boil take off heat then add 3/4 cup of semi-sweet chocolate chip. Mix til smooth. Put in piping bag. Pipe an amount around the the edge of the cookie then fill the Center with 1/4 tsp of raspberry jam. Delicious!

Excellent recipe as written. I did follow the measure of ingredients, however, I did use a 3x2.5" egg shaped cutter for Easter cookies so I did a "test" cookie as always. I baked them at 350 F for 11 minutes on parchment paper in a gas oven and let them cool 2 minutes before transferring to a rack. I rolled out the dough between 2 sheets of parchment paper, (no flour needed), with "roller guides" under the parchment which allowed the cookies to be all exactly the same thickness. I used 2 pieces of flat wood molding, 18" long by .25" thick by 1.5" wide. I did chill the dough in between baking batches. I worked with 1/4 of the dough at a time and this recipe, using my cutter, yielded 25 cookies. Beautiful results. The next time I make them I may add some Cream Cheese Baker's Emulsion to intensify the cream cheese flavor. Truly as written, this proved to be an excellent cookie recipe.
Oh, I only chilled the dough for 3 hours. I did cream the butter, sugar then added the egg followed by the extracts and then of course the flour...Perfect!

With all of our changes - this is as an option - I used Lemon Extract for a fresh PoP of flavor to the Cream Cheese - worked very nicely! ALSO, divide into 3 - wrap & press into a thin "saucer" plate size portion & stick in the freezer - once firm - roll 1 at a time - delicious cookie without icing! (forgo the 8 hour chill time too!)

I used 8 oz. cream cheese, 1 tsp vanilla, 1/2 tsp almond extract, 1 egg, 1 tsp baking powder, 1 cup salted butter, 3 1/2 cups flour (ran out of regular flour so 1 1/2 cups of the flour were whole wheat flour)

They turned out awesome! I rolled out the dough immediately in between parchment paper, left it in the freezer for 15 minutes and then cut out the shapes and placed them back on parchment paper. It took about 10/12 minutes in the over for how thick they were.

This is my go-to recipe for any holiday cut-out cookies except that I double the extracts. If you really want the best results, don't roll your dough out with flour. Stay with me here - divide your dough into quarters and roll one portion out at a time between two sheets of parchment paper leaving the other portions in the fridge. I then transfer the rolled-out dough to the fridge again on a cookie sheet to chill a bit longer. Using this method ensures two things - you're not adding extra flour each time you re-roll your dough, and when it comes time to cut, your dough is cold enough to retain shape during transfer. I frost with a recipe containing powdered sugar, milk (ensures it "crusts" or hardens), corn syrup (keeps it shiny), and almond extract.

I refrigerated the dough for half the time (4 hrs) and it was fine. I made some of them thinner than others, the 1/4" baked nicer than the 1/8" at 9 min baking time coming out golden brown crisp on bottom and soft tops. The 1/8" were crisper overall with darker brown bottom and edges. Also used salted butter. Flavor is very nice.

Amazingly flaky and tender! Great flavor and not too sweet! One adjustment I did make was increasing the flour to 2.5 cups, but otherwise, I followed the recipe to a “T” and the turned out beautifully! Anyone know a good cream cheese frosting that sets up a little firm?

Nicest flavor I've ever tasted in a sugar cookie--I used the alternate recipe version some readers suggested with 4 oz cream cheese, etc. Did notice that the one batch of cookies that I overbaked a bit (light brown edges) tasted better than the barely brown edged cookies--and they were just slightly crisp, not hard (rolled dough at 1/8" thick).
These are all I'll ever make for Christmas cookies! Awesome!
I do the sprinkles and egg white. I find it has enough sweetness without the frosting.
Basically the same as my family recipe, but now my granddaughter has an egg allergy. I've tried a couple substitutes, but they're not the same. Any ideas?
